title: Cap. VIII Resp.: human mass of merited damnation; Augustine De bono persever. 8; Rom. 9:20
pass_a_gloss: But let us descend from angels unto men. I say therefore that in men the equity of this matter can be much more easily perceived than in angels. For since the universal mass of the human race has flowed down into the state of merited damnation by the disobedience of our first parent, if God with no further respect unto actual sins wills to pass by and reject howsoever many in the preparation and donation of special grace, he passes by and rejects those in whom he finds nothing on account of which they should be elected unto participating in so excellent a benefit, and in whom he finds many things on account of which they are judged most unworthy of such a benefit. Nothing else remains to be said here besides that of Augustine, Let him who is freed love grace; let him who is not freed acknowledge the debt, On the Good of Perseverance chapter 8. And that of the Apostle, Rom. 9:20. O man, who art thou that answerest God? Shall the thing formed say, etc.
pass_b_english: Descend from angels to men. In men the equity of this is far easier to see. Since the whole mass of humankind has flowed down into merited damnation by our first parent's disobedience, if God with no further regard to actual sins wills to pass by and reject however many in preparing and giving special grace, he passes by and rejects those in whom he finds nothing for which they should be elect to so excellent a benefit, and in whom he finds much for which they are most unworthy of it. Nothing else need be said but Augustine (On the Good of Perseverance 8): Let him who is freed love grace; let him who is not freed acknowledge the debt — and Paul (Rom. 9:20): O man, who are you to answer God? Shall the thing formed say...?
source_text: Sed ab angelis ad homines descendamus. Dico igitur in hominibus hujus rei aequitatem multo facilius perspici posse quam in angelis. Nam cum universa massa humani generis in statum meritae damnationis defluxerit primi parentis nostri inobedientia, si Deus nullo ulteriore ad peccata actualia respectu praeterire et rejicere velit quamvis multos in praeparatione et donatione gratiae specialis, praeterit et rejicit eos, in quibus nihil invenit propter quod ad tam eximium beneficium participandum eligantur, et in quibus multa invenit propter quae tali beneficio indignissimi censeantur. Nihil aliud hic dicendum restat praeter illud Augustini, Qui liberatur, gratiam diligat; qui non liberatur, debitum agnoscat, De bono persever. cap. 8. Et illud Apostoli, Rom. ix. 20. O homo, tu quis es qui respondeas Deo? Num dicet figmentum, etc.
